AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: This study examined differences in health risks and workplace outcomes among employees who utilized preventive dental services compared with other employees.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A retrospective observational study of employees of a large financial services corporation, with data from health risk appraisal questionnaires, medical claims, pharmacy claims, and dental claims.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Employees with no dental claims were significantly more likely to have a variety of health risk factors (such as obesity and tobacco use), health conditions (such as diabetes), absenteeism, and lost on-the-job productivity, and were significantly less likely to be compliant with clinical preventive services compared with those with preventive dental claims.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Employees with preventive dental claims had fewer health risks and medical conditions and better health and productivity measures. Study employees underutilized free dental care; employers should incorporate preventive dental care awareness into their worksite wellness programs.
